alignments.note: Verbless Greek clause with a noun-phrase predicate: under rules 53 and 63 the supplied copula stays with the subject pronoun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Adverbial phrase renders the single particle; head on the meaning-bearing word under rule 17.

Second verbless clause expresses no subject of its own, so the predicate carries the supplied copula under rule 68; the Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is a rule 51 helper on the noun. Giving the copula to the relative pronoun of the first clause remains defensible.
Case preposition rides with the noun under rules 21 and 17.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else under rule 32.

One Greek verb rendered by a light-verb phrase; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement, as bear witness heads on witness. Auxiliary rides along under rule 9, discontinuously past the negative under rule 15.
Light-verb rendering headed on the meaning-bearing complement under rule 17.
